name: Loose Object Hazard Detection
disclaimer: Real-camera demo experiment. Every expectedObjects entry is a class the loaded YOLOv8n COCO-80 model can actually detect (person, bottle, cell phone, knife, ...). The experiment NEVER uses pen / red_box / yellow_box / experiment_box / target_area — those require a custom-trained model (see backend/experiments/README). The hazard side comes from the config-driven hazards.json knowledge base, not from this sequence.
description: A controlled loose-object hazard scene: the astronaut is in view (normal scene), a loose bottle appears, a second loose object (cell phone) appears, a sharp object (knife) appears, then a multi-object scene. The safety monitor (not the experiment state machine) is what escalates CAUTION/WARNING/CRITICAL and opens alerts.

steps.label: Normal scene — astronaut in view
steps.description: The astronaut is detected. Detection list is populated and the safe percentage updates; no hazard alert is expected.

steps.label: Loose bottle introduced into the scene
steps.description: A bottle is moved into the monitored area. The safety monitor assesses it as a possible free-floating-object hazard (CAUTION/WARNING depending on persistence/proximity) and opens an alert when confirmed.

steps.label: Second loose object introduced
steps.description: A cell phone joins the scene so multiple independent objects are tracked and assessed simultaneously.

steps.label: Sharp object introduced
steps.description: A knife enters the scene. The safety monitor treats it as a sharp-object hazard candidate (CRITICAL per hazards.json) — demonstrated as an emergency-escalation example, confirmed only after persistence.

steps.label: Multi-object scene
steps.description: Astronaut plus bottle, cell phone and knife appear simultaneously. All supported objects appear in the detection list and each carries its own hazard assessment.

steps.label: Scene cleared — back to normal
steps.description: The loose and sharp objects are removed; only the astronaut remains. Terminal step.

validationRules.nextExpectedOnError: unchanged - the offending step must be performed again to advance
validationRules.skippedStepEvidence: SKIPPED_STEP is advisory and is only emitted together with OUT_OF_SEQUENCE; progress advances exclusively on STEP_MATCHED

errorTypes.when: detected activity equals the expected step
known activity from a later step is detected before the expected step
advisory emitted together with OUT_OF_SEQUENCE (a later step implies earlier steps were skipped)
known activity from an already-completed step is detected again
detected activity is null or not defined in this experiment
detected activity confidence is below the validationRules.lowConfidenceThreshold
errorTypes.progressEffect: none - treat the detection as uncertain

example.note: The sequence advances only when the actual scene matches the expected step; the safety monitor runs independently and assesses whatever is actually detected.
